body:
AMEND — one remaining contract failure under the anti-dither rule.

Boundary payloads are now owned by C1-E; the native timestamp envelope and D2 refusals by C1-B; source/admission authority is excluded from C1; compiler, codec, accepted-claim and provider integration remain later; C1-F correctly limits legacy conformance to an in-memory result; and every child has portable JVM/JS/Native laws. Those earlier findings are incorporated.

The remaining failure is the B0-C dependency. This amendment allows C1-T to freeze the complete public inventory after D2 alone, while the anti-dither sequence instantiates aggregate B0 later and exercises the synthetic fixture only after C1. B0-C owns the normative two-acquisition-run repair specification and synthetic input/expected-output oracle. Freezing C1 types before that oracle is accepted, then testing the oracle only after C1-F closes, permits a required lawful reset/gap/occurrence or set-valued reverse case to be unrepresentable in a supposedly closed API. That is criterion (b), and it also weakens the promised reproducibility court.

Minimal repair: require accepted B0-C specification plus exact oracle identity before C1-T closes; bind that oracle into the C1-T constructor/refusal matrix; and require the generic ClockRepair/TrackComposition implementation to pass it on JVM/JS/Native before aggregate C1 closes. This does not require aggregate B0 rights closure, any source read, or D0. Aggregate B0 plus P1 may continue to block C1-A production edits exactly as stated. D0 remains the first exact source reader and emits the realized source-specific repair receipt.

No other contract failure remains.
